findings.title: Sender/user check is skipped entirely for new installations
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when no Integration exists for the installation_id, the `except Integration.DoesNotExist` branch at line 482 returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately. The new check that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` (lines 493-505) is therefore only reached for pre-existing Integrations. The first-time install, which is the main path the PR is meant to protect, never validates the authenticated user against the app installer. The PR description says the pipeline should fail on a user mismatch, but for new installs it will proceed regardless of who completed OAuth.

findings.title: KeyError when the existing Integration has no sender in metadata
findings.body: The check at lines 501-505 indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly. `build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (integration.py around line 376), so Integrations created without a sender (or with metadata lacking it) raise KeyError and turn the install step into a 500. Also `fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` may be None if the OAuth step was skipped, which would then be compared as a mismatch with no clear error. This should use `.get()` with an explicit failure path.

findings.title: Network failure in the token exchange is unhandled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(url=..., data=data)` at line 423 is outside the try block that guards only the body read and parse. If GitHub is unreachable or times out, the exception propagates and the user gets a 500 instead of the friendly invalid-installation error. The same applies to `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` at line 434, which is also not guarded. Both calls should be wrapped so failures route to `error(...)`.

findings.title: code parameter is not validated before the token exchange
findings.body: `data["code"]` is taken from `request.GET.get("code")` (line 417) and may be None when the GitHub callback lacks a code. The request is still sent to GitHub with an empty code. This is harmless only because GitHub rejects it, but it causes a needless external call and makes the failure mode depend on GitHub's response rather than an explicit check.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 path
findings.body: The test was changed so the second request uses a mismatched state (`ddd023...`), so it now fails at the state check in OAuthLoginView and asserts only the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message. The original assertion for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' from build_integration's 404 handling is gone, and nothing else covers that branch anymore. The test should send a matching state and assert the 404-specific message.

findings.title: No test covers a successful user match for an existing integration or a new install without sender
findings.body: The new tests only cover the mismatch path (test_github_user_mismatch) and the state-mismatch case. There is no test asserting that a matching authenticated user succeeds when an Integration already exists with a sender, and none for a first-time install, which is the path where the check is skipped. Tests also depend on hard-coded `responses.calls[2]` indices (line 257 in assert_setup_flow), which makes them fragile to any change in the number of HTTP calls.

findings.title: Unrelated removal of the FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR module constant
findings.body: The diff removes the public module-level constant `FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR` and inlines `provider_id == "github"`. This change is not part of the stated security fix. If any other module imports this constant it will break, and the inlining makes it harder to extend to other providers. It should be split into a separate change or kept as is.
